sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic Languages. Richmond: Curzon.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mondropolon appears only in the listing of Oceanic languages by subgroup (Mid West Manus linkage, p.879). The only stress remark is the family-wide typological generalization (p.35/§3.1: 'Stress is generally fully predictable, falling on the penultimate syllable of a word') which is not specific to Mondropolon.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, Special Issue 2021. Front matter / Table of contents / Introduction (18 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Mondropolon. Table 0.1 (p.13) lists Mondropolon as language 23 of Blust's 1975 survey with only 4 contact hours over 2 days; it is not among the eight languages sketched (Seimat, Bipi, Lindrou, Sori, Likum, Loniu, Pak, Nauna). Only stress mentions in the file are TOC entries for the Lindrou sketch (Table 3.2, 3.10).

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands. Sketch 2: Bipi; Sketch 5: Likum. LLM Special Issue 2021.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology sections are for Likum/Bipi only; Mondropolon is mentioned solely as sharing the coda *t > -k change (Bipi sketch p.158) and the majority numeral pattern (Likum sketch). No Mondropolon stress statement.

sources.note: Mondropolon indexed at pp. xxxiii, 101 (one of the smallest AN languages), 231 (has contrastive medial geminates), 636 (palatal glide epenthesis before *a). Nothing on stress.
